STEP 1 - Scene: A small side salad of mixed leafy greens (looks like arugula/rocket and similar leaves) with thin shreds of carrot. No dressing is clearly visible.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square-ish white bowl/dish, roughly 22 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (11)^2 ≈ 380 cm² (treating it as a round equivalent; a square of 22 cm would be 484 cm², so I use the middle estimate of ~400 cm²).

STEP 3 - Items: (a) mixed leafy greens (arugula-type), (b) shredded carrot.

STEP 4 - Area: Greens cover about 17% of the vessel area. Carrot shreds are sparse, about 1% of the area, mostly inside the greens pile.
Total food coverage ≈ 18% of vessel area.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Greens: 17% of 400 cm² ≈ 68 cm² x 4 cm height ≈ 272 ml.
- Carrot: 1% ≈ 4 cm² x 1 cm ≈ 4 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Greens: 272 ml x 0.15 g/ml ≈ 41 g.
- Carrot: 4 ml x 0.6 g/ml ≈ 2 g.
Total ≈ 43 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Leafy greens: 41 g x 25 kcal/100 g ≈ 10 kcal.
- Carrot: 2 g x 41 kcal/100 g ≈ 1 kcal.
Total ≈ 11 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A modest bowl of loose salad greens with a few carrot shreds, no dressing visible, should weigh a few tens of grams and be low in energy. About 43 g and roughly 11 kcal fits. If a dressing were added, the energy would rise considerably, but none is visible.
